transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora. I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any left, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that makes sense. I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay, so it would be worth mentioning to your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago. I don't have any more questions right now. Thank you for all the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you answered all my questions. I appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! I'm so glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery!

verdict.label: pass
